gloss: going up and down; ascent and descent

definitions.gloss: going up and down; ascent and descent
definitions.explanation: The physical act of going uphill and downhill, or ascending and descending. Used for slopes, stairs, and roads.
Figurative use referring to fluctuations, variations, or instability in conditions, prices, or emotions.

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This road has many ups and downs.

examples.japanese: {階段|かいだん}の{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りだけで{息|いき}が{切|き}れる。
examples.english: Just going up and down the stairs leaves me out of breath.

examples.japanese: {山道|やまみち}の{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}しながら、やっと{頂上|ちょうじょう}に{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: After repeatedly going up and down mountain paths, we finally reached the summit.

examples.japanese: {株価|かぶか}の{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りが{激|はげ}しい。
examples.english: The stock price fluctuations are intense.

examples.japanese: {気温|きおん}の{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りが{大|おお}きくて、{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}しやすい。
examples.english: The large temperature fluctuations make it easy to get sick.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}には{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りがあるものだから、{落|お}ち{込|こ}みすぎないほうがいい。
examples.english: Life has its ups and downs, so it's better not to get too depressed.

notes:
USAGE:
{上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}り describes both literal vertical movement and figurative fluctuations. The literal sense is common when talking about terrain, stairs, or slopes, while the figurative sense applies to prices, temperatures, and life circumstances.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りが{多|おお}い (has many ups and downs)
- {上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りが{激|はげ}しい (has extreme fluctuations)
- {上|のぼ}り{下|くだ}りを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す (to repeatedly go up and down)
